haiku-low.q1: Pages of 500 in id order (keyset), fetched one at a time. Nothing is fetched in parallel.
haiku-low.q2: In sync_state as staging_last_saved_id, committed in the same SQLite transaction as the page's staging rows.
haiku-low.q3: Watermark is taken first, so pages hold everything up to it. Later edits arrive via the change feed catch-up from the watermark.
haiku-low.q4: Server returns 410 resync_required when after_seq is below oldest_valid_seq. Catch-up discards staging and takes a new watermark; incremental resyncs with live copy kept.
haiku-low.q5: Built in a new staging generation beside the live one, with no copying. One transaction flips live_generation to it once catch-up finishes; old rows are cleaned up later.
haiku-low.q6: App launch, return to foreground, or Wi-Fi regained. It runs if a live catalogue exists, no staging is active, and 15 minutes passed since the last incremental run started.
haiku-low.q7: Retries the same request after waits of 2, 4, 8, 16 s, five attempts total. Then stops, keeps all saved data, and waits for the next trigger.
haiku-low.q8: It finishes the in-flight page, saves it, then pauses and starts no new request on cellular. It resumes on Wi-Fi with the attempt counter reset.
haiku-low.q9: For change-feed records, it applies the record only if its incoming change_seq is at least the stored one. Page-row handling is only stated as upserts.
haiku-low.q10: It starts at live_cursor_seq and moves to next_seq after each committed batch of changes.
haiku-low.q11: It reads each product row's latest change_seq, so one entry per product. Deletes appear as deleted: true tombstones.

sonnet.q1: Paged with keyset pagination: GET /products?after_id=<opaque>&limit=500, ordered by id ascending, tombstones excluded, about 500 products (~1 MB) per page, 800 pages for 400,000 products. Pages (and changes) are never fetched in parallel; one request at a time.
sonnet.q2: In the SQLite sync_state row as staging_last_saved_id. Each page's rows are written to the staging generation as upserts and staging_last_saved_id is set to last_id in one SQLite transaction, so they are always committed together.
sonnet.q3: The client first records a watermark (highest committed change_seq) and saves it before fetching pages. After the pages finish, it replays the change feed from the watermark into staging (catch-up). Edits before the watermark are in the pages; later edits (new lower-id products, changes, deletes as tombstones) come through the feed, which has no gaps. A product deleted before its page was fetched is not returned, and its feed entry is a no-op.
sonnet.q4: The server answers 410 {error: "resync_required"} (when after_seq < oldest_valid_seq), never a partial feed. The client does not retry it: during incremental sync it goes to resync (a new staging full download while the live catalogue stays visible); during catch-up it discards staging and restarts at step 2 with a fresh watermark.
sonnet.q5: It is built as a new staging generation beside the live one: watermark, pages, then catch-up, all into staging while reps keep using the live copy. It becomes the one the app reads when, in one transaction, live_generation is set to staging_generation (and live_cursor_seq to staging_cursor_seq), a pointer flip with nothing copied, after catch-up has_more is false. Old generations are cleaned up afterward.
sonnet.q6: Triggers: app launch, return to foreground (Wi-Fi regained also triggers the router), when there is a live generation and no staging in progress. It runs at most once every 15 minutes, measured from the start of the last incremental run (including a failed one); if the device clock moved backwards the interval is treated as elapsed. Any network is allowed.
sonnet.q7: Repeat the same request unchanged, retrying after waits of 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, then 16 s: at most 5 attempts in total (about 30 s of waiting). After the 5th failure, stop, keep everything already saved (nothing rolled back), and wait for the next trigger. The attempt counter is in memory and resets on each new trigger.
sonnet.q8: The request in flight is allowed to finish and its page is saved, then the download pauses; no new request starts on cellular. This is not a failure. When Wi-Fi returns, it resumes from staging_last_saved_id and resets the attempt counter. (The catch-up step may use any network.)
sonnet.q9: For upserts in catch-up, the client applies the change only when the incoming change_seq is at least the stored row's change_seq (deletes are applied the same way, and a missing row is a no-op). For incremental sync on the live generation, the document says only that upserts are applied and deletes remove the row; no comparison is stated there. Page rows are written as upserts.
sonnet.q10: It starts from live_cursor_seq: GET /changes?after_seq=<live_cursor_seq>&limit=1000. The cursor moves forward to the response's next_seq in the same transaction that applies each response's changes, continuing while has_more is true. After a resync going live, live_cursor_seq is set from staging_cursor_seq.
sonnet.q11: It reads product rows by their change_seq (the global increasing version stamped at commit, indexed), ordered by change_seq, at most 1,000 per response; each product has only its latest change_seq so the feed shows the latest version of each changed product, not history. Deletes are soft-delete tombstones (deleted = true, kept 7 days) and appear in the feed as entries with deleted: true.
